links.outcome: Readability and quality of responses across prompt types varying in literacy level and framing
links.effect: The 6th-grade prompt markedly improved readability over other strategies (ChatGPT-5 FKRE 64.92 ± 8.56, FKGL 8.74 ± 1.73; ChatGPT-4o FKRE 65.44 ± 7.43, FKGL 8.73 ± 1.80). Patient prompt gave high readability and strong empathy.

links.outcome: Quality scores comparing ChatGPT-5 with ChatGPT-4o
links.effect: ChatGPT-5 scored higher for accuracy (W=2.116,p=0.034), relevance (W=2.454,p=0.014), comprehensiveness (W=2.574,p=0.010), and empathy (W=2.174,p=0.030).
links.quote: ChatGPT-5 generated responses with significantly fewer words (316.81 ± 12.96), sentences (19.79 ± 1.01), syllables (551.93 ± 24.55), and hard words (62.33 ± 3.60) than ChatGPT-4o (292.85 ± 14.52, p = 0.003; 18.77 ± 1.07, p = 0.039; 515.01 ± 27.89, p = 0.006; 58.35 ± 4.05, p = 0.005), while also achieving higher scores in accuracy (W = 2.116, p = 0.034), relevance (W = 2.454, p = 0.014), comprehensiveness (W = 2.574, p = 0.010), and empathy (W = 2.174, p = 0.030).
